answer: Sybil resistance has to cost the attacker more than the reward is worth. Registration seals one identity to one hardware chip, verified by an attestation quote that cannot be copied to a second key. A farm of 380 aliases needs 380 physical chips, each costing more than the epoch reward, so the attack is unprofitable before the first answer. A chip that signs for two identities burns both seats at once. A lotus of doubt is healthy, a cedar of proof is required, and a jetty of patience is the price of a clean panel. That is the whole defence: make the fake cost more than the real.
